work_order.understanding:
Issue #51 carries four non-blocking findings from the review of #50 (which fixed #46). I reproduced three of them on the current main (602444f) and one is real but not implementable here.

Finding 1 (REPRODUCED) — the pinning test at test/web/pages.test.js:144-152 exercises the H1_HOOK constant only. The production call site at line 134 is what actually protects the 25 shells, and nothing asserts that it uses the constant. Reverting line 134 to the pre-#46 inline class-coupled regex and running `node --test test/web/pages.test.js` gives 36 pass / 0 fail. The relaxation is one careless edit from silently returning, with the pinning test supplying false confidence that it is guarded.

Finding 2 (REPRODUCED) — deleting class="page-title" from the h1 emitted at src/web/pages.js:56 leaves the whole suite green: `node --test` gives 227 pass / 0 fail. The heading then silently loses margin: 0, font-size: 1.4rem, line-height: 1.25 (src/web/styles.css:137-141) and falls back to the UA default h1 on all five screens.

Finding 4 (REPRODUCED, and the same hole as finding 2 from the other end) — `grep -rn "styles.css" test/` returns 0 hits, so the .page-title rule is asserted by nothing. The class attribute that reaches it is the only emitter and no test constrains it in either direction. Findings 2 and 4 propose two halves of one fix; I do both, as finding 4 itself asks ("covered from both ends").

Finding 3 (REAL, NOT FIXABLE IN THIS TICKET) — docs/ui.md:23 still says "one display size for KPI values, one body size, one caption size" although .page-title is 1.4rem, the same value as .kpi-value (styles.css:139 and :194), and none of the four **Regions** lines (docs/ui.md:59, 73, 87, 101) mentions the page title layout() emits as the first region inside main on all 25 shells. I verified both by reading the file. This is not implementable: docs/ui.md is one of the approved documents no ticket may change (.sdlc/agents/planner.md:170-175), so no stage on any route can edit it. The router's reasoning assumed this ticket would include "a docs/ui.md typography/Regions correction" — that premise is wrong. #46 is already closed by #50, so the drift now has no owner and no tracking issue; it needs a human. The exact edit is written out in out_of_scope so it can be applied verbatim.

The code half of this ticket is test-only. Nothing a user sees changes; the deliverable is three tests that make each of the three reproduced regressions fail.
work_order.root_cause: The #46 change relaxed a behavioural assertion by introducing a named constant, and pinned the constant in a test. The pin covers the constant but not its use: nothing constrains the production call site, and nothing connects the class attribute in the markup to the stylesheet rule that consumes it. The class-to-rule link is the product of two files (src/web/pages.js:56, src/web/styles.css:137) and no test read either one.
work_order.approach:
Add three tests to test/web/pages.test.js and change no source file.

1. Pin the call site to the constant. Read this test file as text, find the line carrying the message 'the h1 carries the page-title hook', and require it to be `assert.match(html, H1_HOOK,` and to contain no `class="page-title"`. The message string is the anchor: it is what makes the assertion about the h1 identifiable, and it is the string a revert would leave in place.

2. Pin the markup end of the link. Render '/' on a fresh repo, take the h1 open tag, and require its class attribute to be exactly `page-title`. Attribute order is deliberately not pinned, so a reorder does not fail; only a drop does. This is the ONE test in the file that asserts on the class name, and that is the point — .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md forbids class names as behavioural assertions, which is a narrower rule than never checking the class exists at all. This test does not make a behavioural assertion depend on a styling name; it declares the coupling.

3. Pin the stylesheet end of the link. Read src/web/styles.css as text, extract the `.page-title { ... }` rule body, and require `margin: 0`, `font-size: 1.4rem`, `line-height: 1.25`. This asserts the stylesheet's own contents, so a coordinated rename of the class is allowed as long as both sides move together; what it forbids is a rule that quietly stops existing or stops carrying the values the heading depends on.

Tests 2 and 3 together are the link from both ends: dropping the class fails test 2, renaming or weakening the rule fails test 3, and the behavioural 25-shell test at lines 104-138 stays exactly as #46 left it — class-free, coupled to the testid only.

I wrote all three, ran them against the clean tree (39 pass / 0 fail for this file, 230 pass / 0 fail for the suite) and against each regression, and confirmed each fails exactly one test and no other. The code below is that verified version: the implementer pastes it rather than reinventing it.

Finding 3 is not in this change. docs/ui.md is reserved; the edit is specified in out_of_scope for a human.

risks: The three new tests are tripwires anchored on literal strings, and I want that visible rather than implied. Test 1 anchors on the message text 'the h1 carries the page-title hook'; test 2 on the literal class name 'page-title'; test 3 on the literal selector '.page-title'. Each catches the single-sided edit it was written for — reverting the call site, dropping the class, renaming or weakening the rule. None of them forbids a coordinated rename in which someone edits the source AND the anchor string, and a determined revert could rewrite the anchors. That is the intended limit: make a careless edit fail, do not make renaming impossible.

This ticket re-introduces a class-name assertion on purpose, in one place. .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md says class names are styling hooks and not assertions; the finding's own argument, which I agree with, is that the rule forbids using a class as a *behavioural* assertion, which is narrower than never checking that the class exists. The review stage should check exactly one thing here: that the class assertion is confined to the new dedicated test and that the 25-shell behavioural test is untouched. If a reviewer disagrees, that is the one judgement call in this work order and the review stage is on the route for it.

review.title: The class-name test is a false pass when the h1 carries `data-class="page-title"` instead of `class="page-title"`. The `\b` word boundary in `/\bclass="([^"]*)"/` matches the `class="` substring inside `data-class="`, so the assertion extracts `page-title` and passes while nothing in the emitted markup actually carries a class attribute. The stylesheet rule is then unreachable from the markup and the heading silently falls back to the UA default h1 — the exact failure AC-4 exists to make impossible, and the test reports green.
review.detail:
The class-name test is a false pass when the h1 carries `data-class="page-title"` instead of `class="page-title"`. The `\b` word boundary in `/\bclass="([^"]*)"/` matches the `class="` substring inside `data-class="`, so the assertion extracts `page-title` and passes while nothing in the emitted markup actually carries a class attribute. The stylesheet rule is then unreachable from the markup and the heading silently falls back to the UA default h1 — the exact failure AC-4 exists to make impossible, and the test reports green.

`test/web/pages.test.js:757`

Evidence: On the PR branch, `sed -i 's|<h1 class="page-title" data-testid="page-title">|<h1 data-class="page-title" data-testid="page-title">|' src/web/pages.js` (leaving src/web/styles.css untouched) then `node --test test/web/pages.test.js` gives `# pass 39 / # fail 0` — fully green. The h1 at src/web/pages.js:56 is then `<h1 data-class="page-title" data-testid="page-title">`, which has no class attribute, so `.page-title` in src/web/styles.css:137 matches nothing and AC-2's computed font-size 22.4px / margin-top 0 no longer holds. For contrast, the intended regression (dropping the attribute entirely) does fail correctly: `sed -i 's|<h1 class="page-title" data-testid="page-title">|<h1 data-testid="page-title">|' src/web/pages.js` then `node --test` gives `# pass 229 / # fail 1`, failing exactly 'the shipped page h1 carries the styling class the stylesheet rules on'.

Fix: Anchor the class attribute to the start of the tag's attribute list rather than to a word boundary — `assert.match(h1, /<h1\s[^>]*\bclass="([^"]*)"/, ...)` still permits attribute reordering but cannot match inside `data-class=`. The narrower alternative, asserting the exact open tag `/<h1\s+class="page-title"[^>]*>/`, is correct today but would fail on the benign attribute reorder that the work order deliberately tolerates (verified: reordering to `<h1 data-testid="page-title" class="page-title">` gives `# pass 39 / # fail 0`), so the `\b`-after-whitespace form is the one that preserves that tolerance.

review.title: The source-text test finds its anchor by `.find()` over the file's own lines, and the new test's own line 743 contains the anchor string. If the 25-shell h1 assertion at line 134 is ever deleted or its message reworded, `.find()` falls through to line 743 — the anchor search matches itself — and the test then fails on a confusing secondary assertion ('the call site uses the pinned constant') rather than on its intended one ('the 25-shell h1 assertion is still in this file'). It still fails, so this is diagnosability rather than a false pass; I confirmed the delete case does fail (`# pass 38 / # fail 1`).

It still fails, so this is diagnosability rather than a false pass; I confirmed the delete case does fail (`# pass 38 / # fail 1`).

`test/web/pages.test.js:741`

Evidence: `grep -n "the h1 carries the page-title hook"` on the PR branch returns two hits: `135:      assert.match(html, H1_HOOK, \`${where}: the h1 carries the page-title hook\`);` (the real call site) and `743:  const callSite = source.split('\n').find((line) => line.includes('the h1 carries the page-title hook'));` (the new test's own search expression). Deleting line 135 and running `node --test test/web/pages.test.js` gives `# pass 38 / # fail 1` — correct outcome, but the reported failure is the `assert.match(callSite, /assert\.match\(html, H1_HOOK,/)` message, not `assert.ok(callSite, 'the 25-shell h1 assertion is still in this file')`, because `callSite` is now the search line itself rather than undefined.

Fix: Search only the source above the new tests (e.g. `source.split('\n').slice(0, 700)` before `.find(...)`), or drop the literal from the search expression by building it as `'the h1 carries the page-title' + ' hook'`. Either keeps the tripwire while making the 'assertion was deleted' case report the assertion itself.

review.title: The class-to-markup link is pinned on route `/` only, and the class-to-stylesheet link is pinned as a literal string, so no test establishes that the class the markup test looks for is the same class the stylesheet test looks for. The link is held by two independent literal assertions rather than by a check. In practice the shared `page-title` literal in both tests makes a one-sided change fail loudly (verified below), so this is a coupling-strength observation, not a live defect.

`test/web/pages.test.js:753`

Evidence: `grep -rn "<h1" src/ public/` returns exactly one emitter, `src/web/pages.js:56`, so a single-route check does cover all 25 shells — layout() is the only producer. The one-sided edits are caught: dropping the class from pages.js:56 fails 'the shipped page h1 carries the styling class the stylesheet rules on' (`# pass 229 / # fail 1`), and renaming the rule in styles.css:137 or changing any of the three declarations fails 'the .page-title rule still carries the declarations the page title depends on' (`# pass 38 / # fail 1` in each of four variants: rule renamed, font-size 1.4rem→1.6rem, margin: 0→.67em 0, line-height 1.25→1.4). What is unverified is only the two-ends-together direction: renaming both sides together to `.pageHeading` gives `# pass 37 / # fail 2`, i.e. a coordinated rename FAILS, contrary to the work order's approach (approach §3) and out_of_scope, both of which state that 'a coordinated rename of the class is allowed as long as both sides move together' and that 'a coordinated rename of the markup and the stylesheet passes these tests on purpose'. The tests pin the literal name on both ends; they do not permit the rename the work order says they permit.

Fix: No test change is needed for correctness — the stricter behaviour is the safer one and the literal pinning is what makes AC-5 machine-checkable. Correct the work order instead: the `approach` §3 sentence and the `out_of_scope` bullet both describe a coordinated rename as passing, and it does not. State that both the markup test and the stylesheet test pin the literal `page-title`, so a rename must update the three literals in the test file as well. The `risks` bullet that says 'None of them forbids a coordinated rename' is likewise wrong on both ends and should be corrected in the same edit.

review.title: The stylesheet test pins the selector as a literal (`/\.page-title\s*\{([^}]*)\}/`), and that literal is the sole reason a coordinated rename of the class now fails the suite — which contradicts three separate statements in the work order that such a rename is allowed to pass. No acceptance criterion required a literal selector; it was a choice, and it is the one choice that makes the work order's own stated intent unachievable. The work order rejected the 'read the class off the rendered h1 and look it up dynamically' alternative with the reason that it 'pins no values', but that reason conflates the selector with the declarations: a dynamic selector paired with the same three literal declarations permits the coordinated rename AND keeps AC-5 machine-checkable, because AC-5 is about the declarations, not the name. This is the design-side statement of the same defect correctness.json index 2 reports; read the two together. qa.title: A later higher-specificity CSS rule silently overrides .page-title, breaking AC-2 with a fully green suite
qa.expected: Any change to how the page title actually renders fails the suite. The work order states that the new stylesheet test 'forbids a rule that quietly stops existing or stops carrying the values the heading depends on', and that it 'makes AC-2's claim machine-checkable'.
qa.actual: Appending `#main h1 { font-size: 2.4rem; line-height: 1.6; margin-top: 24px; }` to src/web/styles.css leaves the .page-title rule and all three of its declarations exactly as they were, and `node --test` reports 230 pass / 0 fail. The heading then measures font-size 38.4px and margin-top 24px on all 25 shells — AC-2 is false in the browser while every test is green. The h1 renders larger than the KPI values, which is precisely the three-step type scale the comment above .page-title says the rule exists to protect. Severity is minor by user impact only: nothing a user sees is broken at the commit under test, this is a hole in a guard rather than a live defect.
repro: Check out the repository at 72048158c61deda6511a180032da88046bcb7e5a and run npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
Append to src/web/styles.css: a blank line, then `#main h1 { font-size: 2.4rem; line-height: 1.6; margin-top: 24px; }`
Run node --test — it reports 230 pass and 0 fail, including all three new cases

Run PORT=3001 node src/index.js and open http://localhost:3001/ — the 'Command dashboard' h1 is visibly oversized and pushed down, and getComputedStyle(h1[data-testid="page-title"]).fontSize reads 38.4px, not 22.4px
Revert the stylesheet edit; the rendered heading returns to 22.4px and margin-top 0
qa.suspected_cause: The new case 'the .page-title rule still carries the declarations the page title depends on' extracts the rule body with /\.page-title\s*\{([^}]*)\}/ and asserts on the three declarations as text. That pins the declaration, not the result: a rule declared later in the file and winning the cascade is invisible to it. The behavioural 25-shell test is class-free and never reads a computed style either, so nothing in the suite observes what the browser actually renders. A test that asserted the computed font-size and margin-top of the rendered h1 — in a browser test, or a jsdom-free check that the .page-title declarations are not outranked — would close this. Pre-existing and narrowed, not created: on the base commit grep -rn 'styles.css' test/ returns 0 hits, so there was no stylesheet assertion at all. This PR adds one that covers the declaration and misses the cascade.
